findings.excerpt: def toRoot (x : ModularCurve.TateModule p J) : _root_.TateModule p J := ⟨x, mem_root_of_mem x.2⟩
findings.problem: The project has two definitions of the Tate module. `ModularCurve.TateModule p J` is a Hecke submodule of `ℕ → J` defined by `x 0 = 0 ∧ ∀ n, p • x (n+1) = x n`. `_root_.TateModule p M` is an `AddSubgroup` of `ℕ → M` defined by `∀ n, p^n • x n = 0 ∧ p • x (n+1) = x n`. The two carriers are the same set of sequences; `mem_root_of_mem` and `mem_of_mem_root` in this file prove it. Only `_root_.TateModule` has the ℤ_[p]-module structure, `rep`, `proj`, and the finiteness, freeness and rank API. This file therefore adds a bridge (`toRoot`, `ofRoot`, `β`), re-derives the ℤ_[p]-`Module` by pulling back along an injective map, and re-proves `eq_zero_of_smul_eq_zero` and `natCast_smul_apply`. It also re-declares `Module.Free`, `IsTorsionFree` and `Module.Finite` instances for `ModularCurve.TateModule`. The `scoped` instances are visible only to code that opens this namespace. All later results (`ρT`, `tT`, `quadratic_of_root`, `exists_sub_eq_pow_smul_of_root`, `hdiv_jZero`) then repeatedly transport statements back and forth through `β`.
findings.proposed_change: Where `ModularCurve.TateModule` is defined, make it a thin wrapper over the root definition rather than a second concept. For example, define it as the image or comap of `_root_.TateModule` and put `Module ℤ_[p]` and the `HeckeAlg` action there, or state the Hecke-module version as an abbreviation or `Submodule` structure on top of `_root_.TateModule`. Upstream consumers would then get the ℤ_[p]-module structure, `rep` and `proj` directly. At minimum, move `toRoot`, `ofRoot`, `β` and the module instances next to the definitions as a shared API, so that no downstream file has to rebuild the bridge.
findings.benefit: Readers no longer need to track which of two equivalent Tate modules a statement lives in, and the `β` transport lemmas (`ρT_apply`, `tT_apply'`, `quadratic_of_root`, …) mostly disappear. Module, finiteness and freeness instances are defined once instead of per file, and they are no longer hidden behind `scoped`.

findings.declaration: ρA (and hρA, ρA_apply) duplicating ρM (hρ, ρM_apply)
findings.excerpt: def ρA : Γ →* Module.End O'' (O'' ⊗[ℤ_[p]] (ModularCurve.TateModule p J)) :=
findings.problem: `ρA` is `ρM` at `G := Γ`: both are `(Module.End.baseChangeHom ℤ_[p] O'' (ModularCurve.TateModule p J)).toRingHom.toMonoidHom.comp (ρT p J _)`. `ρA_apply` repeats `ρM_apply` and `hρA` repeats `hρ` (the proof is just `hρ O'' σ x y h a`). The generic `ρM` is never used downstream, and `solution` uses only `ρA` and `hρA`. The file therefore carries two parallel names for one base-changed Galois representation, with duplicate API lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: Delete either `ρM`, `ρM_apply` and `hρ` (and state `hρ` for `ρA` directly) or `ρA`, `ρA_apply` and `hρA`. If a named specialisation is wanted, define it as `abbrev ρA := ρM p J Γ O''` so that `ρM_apply` and `hρ` apply to it automatically. The explicit `(p := p) (J := J)` arguments in the `ρA` statements would also become unnecessary.
findings.benefit: There is a single base-change representation to reason about, so `jmap_ρA`, `FA`, `ρres` and `charpoly_galoisRep` can be read without comparing it with an identical generic version. Duplicated lemma statements are removed.
